recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Immediately isolate the affected host from the internal network to prevent any potential lateral movement.
Force a password reset for user *kchen* and enforce multi‑factor authentication (MFA) on all privileged accounts.
Deploy an endpoint detection and response (EDR) agent if not already present, and run a full memory and disk forensic analysis to look for signs of persistence mechanisms or backdoors.

Cross‑reference the source IP (203.0.113.52) against threat intelligence feeds; if it appears on any malicious actor lists, block it at the perimeter firewall and update intrusion detection signatures accordingly.
Review SSH logs from the past 30 days to identify whether this login was an isolated event or part of a broader pattern of compromised credentials.
Conduct a credential stuffing test against the internal authentication system to confirm that the brute‑force attempts were indeed targeting valid accounts.
If any suspicious files or processes are discovered, quarantine them and perform hash‑based comparison with known malware repositories.
Notify relevant stakeholders (SOC, IT security, compliance) of the incident and document all actions taken for audit purposes.
